issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the Y-state preparation function: the problem statement (and tests) require a function named make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, the template repository defines a function named create_y_state(...) (signature at template_repository/msd.py line 41) and its NotImplementedError message references make_y_state, while the reference solution implements make_y_state(...) (solution_repository/msd.py line 95). This mismatch means a student who implements make_y_state as specified by the problem will still find the template lacking that symbol (or automated tests expecting make_y_state may fail), causing import/test failures or confusion about which name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the template's create_y_state(...) to make_y_state(...) (update its signature and the NotImplementedError message) so it matches the problem statement and solution, or add a simple wrapper in the template: def make_y_state(circ, q, p): return create_y_state(circ, q, p). Ensure tests and documentation refer to the single canonical name make_y_state.

issues.description: The concept is preparing a noisy |Y> resource state for injection. The problem statement and tests refer to the function name make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float). The template repository defines a stub named create_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) whose NotImplementedError message mentions make_y_state, and the reference solution implements make_y_state(...). This naming mismatch means a student reading the problem will look to implement make_y_state, but the template provides create_y_state (and tests or autograder may expect make_y_state). The inconsistent identifiers create confusion about which symbol to implement and can cause tests to fail despite correct logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to rename the template stub create_y_state to make_y_state and update its docstring and NotImplementedError message to match. Alternatively, if tests/reference expect create_y_state, update the problem statement and solution to use create_y_state. Ensure the chosen identifier is used consistently in tests, docstrings, error messages, and all code references.
